purpose: Apply the V4 instructional-media framework across the Crew Blueprint knowledge graph without turning visuals into independent technical authority or implying qualification.

authority.rule: A visual inherits the evidence, authority, applicability, review, and publication boundaries of the content it illustrates. A visual never upgrades a claim or grants task authority.

selection_order: Use text alone when no spatial, physical, comparative, or motion variable materially improves understanding.
Use an authentic field photo for recognition of real equipment, work areas, labels, or environmental context.
Use an annotated visual for parts, zones, interfaces, and recognition features.
Use a flow/process diagram for relationships, custody, dependencies, signal/data/material paths, or production handoffs.
Use comparison views for roles, contexts, document types, system layers, or responsibility depth.
Use step sequences only when sequence itself is a learning objective and the task is appropriate for online instructional treatment.
Use video only when motion or changing state is the instructional variable.
Use scenario-choice or micro-practice for judgment/retrieval; these remain separate from scored course assessment.
For controlled/specialist work, prefer recognition, interface, boundary, role, and system-literacy visuals over procedural demonstration.

site_surfaces.media_boundary: Photos and diagrams illustrate recognition and workflow. They do not prescribe site-specific movement, PPE, electrical, rigging, powered-equipment, or structural procedures.
System diagrams remain conceptual unless product/version evidence and responsible review support a more specific representation.
No powered-industrial-truck, machinery, hazardous-material, repair, battery-service, vehicle-operation, or cargo-plan procedure is taught through visuals.

avoid: role imagery that implies credentials or authorization

site_surfaces.release_rule: Any physical-task visual whose correctness depends on exact equipment, product, site, qualified-person judgment, or safety-critical procedure remains owner/practitioner review until the applicable matrix MEDIA/review gates are satisfied.

site_surfaces.controlled_media_rule: Show interface, recognition, ownership, and escalation boundaries; do not use a course visual as an operational procedure for a controlled interface.
Keep platform-specific configuration and controlled-system operation outside unrestricted generic instructional visuals unless exact evidence and review permit it.
Generated or generic visuals must not be presented as manufacturer panel-lock, processing, mapping, calibration, or structural instructions.
Use diagrams to explain system relationships and decision ownership, not to provide structural acceptance or engineered assembly procedure.

site_surfaces.media_boundary: Visuals emphasize item identity, state preservation, discretion, and handoff. They do not prescribe artist-specific setup, tuning, repair, alteration, or performance presets.
Context imagery explains environmental differences; it does not substitute for venue/site rules or current operational instructions.

site_surfaces.data_rule: Volatile employers, openings, pay, market evidence, labor routes, and IATSE/local intake remain Production Atlas-owned. Crew Blueprint visuals may explain stable structures and link outward.

site_surfaces.media_boundary: Management diagrams teach coordination systems; they do not create appointment, signing, engineering, legal, or specialist authority.

site_surfaces.rule: The default online media posture is awareness, system literacy, interface recognition, STOP/ASK/escalation, and external-qualification context.
Source visualizations must preserve direct versus partial versus contextual support and must not imply that bibliography presence equals claim support.

generation_policy.authentic_photos: Prefer authentic current-context photography where physical recognition is the objective and rights/provenance are clear.
generation_policy.generated_photorealistic: May illustrate generic non-authoritative context. Must be labeled illustrative where factual ambiguity is possible and must not masquerade as a manufacturer image, site plan, inspection record, or documentary proof.
generation_policy.generated_diagrams: Preferred for abstract relationships, flows, role maps, and conceptual system architecture when grounded to canonical content/evidence.
generation_policy.external_generation: Any externally generated asset must enter through the same provenance, rights, safety, accessibility, and review gates as internally generated media.

release_invariants: No media asset can upgrade unsupported text into supported evidence.
No safety-critical visual is approved solely because it looks plausible.
No generated technical visual is represented as manufacturer documentation or engineering/site authority.
Every instructional visual has a text equivalent or surrounding explanation sufficient to preserve the learning objective.
Media optimization/CDN delivery is separate from canonical provenance metadata.
Learner clicks on media are not mastery evidence.
